design.holdout: IDs divisible by three were originally reserved before tuning; this is now a previously seen public-training validation cohort, not a fresh hidden test. Both trimaps stay with their image; candidate frozen before the current rerun
design.input: Original native PNGs, decoder checked byte-for-byte against independent Pillow RGBA; grayscale trimap levels explicitly mapped into alpha assets

design.baseline: Previous frozen RGB-aware Galerkin solver and original JS iteration loops, all 36 development cases successful; same native Laplacian, hard labels, tolerance and postprocessing. Compare exact same successful populations. Three-pair throughput study retained separately.
design.convergence: Same original Laplacian, exact hard labels, maximum 2000 CG iterations, actual relative residual <=1e-7, tightened to <=1e-9 with active coarse correction; failures never approximate-success
design.memory: Previous estimated 444-byte reserved-row base retained; optional IC(0) adds 200 bytes/row when it fits. Coarse band/RHS/bookkeeping then optional private WASM vectors/metadata/bookkeeping/prefix/page/transient-chunk estimates fit in spare capacity within the same 192 MiB. Original graph capacity and global JS fallback remain available. GC and whole-process peak memory are not certified by logical graph estimates
design.timing: Individual overlapping container observations, not controlled speed comparisons, p95/input-to-photon, hardware GPU or peak-heap measurements

baseline.metricDefinition:
Local alpha-quality measurements; no official leaderboard compatibility claim.

All alpha values are normalized to [0,1]. Score only the official unknown mask.
Gradient = squared difference of Gaussian-derivative vector fields, sigma 1.4,
nearest-edge extension, scipy truncate=4, sum/1000. Connectivity independently
propagates thresholds 1,0.9,...,0 through prediction and reference from the largest
common exactly opaque component; phi=1-(alpha-level) when alpha-level>=0.15,
lambda=1, absolute phi differences sum/1000. No common opaque source => undefined.
These are explicitly defined local measures inspired by Rhemann et al. CVPR09;
they are not certified replacements for the website/MATLAB implementation.

validation.measurementScope: Paired Node performance study is separate from overlapping corpus/native-browser observations. Photographed browser tests run sequentially after those jobs completed. Queued Hand callback measures only one callback, not gesture p95 or input-to-photon. Whole-process peak heap, physical device and hardware GPU performance are unverified.
validation.loaderRegression: Separate tsImport namespaces reproduced Missing compiled image kernel. Kernel factory/runtime now load through one entry module; actual REST 5355-unknown graph, reference bytes and undo/redo pass.

earlyInterruptedCorpus.reason: Stopped deliberately to fix the discovered REST loader-cache boundary and rerun with corrected worker source hashes; retained separately, never resumed/relabelled as final evidence.

pairedPerformanceStudy.measurement: Three sequential eligible paired runs per input, with alternating version order; Node on this container, not browser/p95/input-to-photon or peak-memory evidence. GT04 pair 1 is retained as warmup/excluded because its baseline overlapped the production build; its replacement is pair 4. GT13 pairs 1-3 and GT04 pairs 2-4 ran without concurrent agent validation workloads. Original baseline solver is a frozen copy with imports rebased and a diagnostic-only host compatibility shim; candidate also includes tighter JS fallback loops. Same native operator, inputs, tolerance and output gates.

import json
from pathlib import Path
import numpy as np
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
root=Path('/tmp/canoli-matting-profile');r=json.loads((root/'paired-final.json').read_text())
plt.rcParams.update({'font.size':10,'axes.spines.top':False,'axes.spines.right':False})
fig,axes=plt.subplots(1,2,figsize=(11,4.6),constrained_layout=True)
for ax,c in zip(axes,r['comparisons']):
 a=np.array(c['baselineSolveMs'])/1000;b=np.array(c['candidateSolveMs'])/1000
 ax.bar([0,1],[np.median(a),np.median(b)],color=['#778590','#55764b'],width=.55)
 ax.scatter(np.zeros(3)+np.linspace(-.1,.1,3),a,s=30,c='#263643',zorder=4)
 ax.scatter(np.ones(3)+np.linspace(-.1,.1,3),b,s=30,c='#21391a',zorder=4)
 ax.set_xticks([0,1],['Previous JS','Private WASM + tighter JS fallback']);ax.set_ylabel('Native solve time (seconds)');ax.set_title(c['id']+' — three eligible pairs\n'+f'Median {np.median(a):.2f} → {np.median(b):.2f} sec ({(np.median(b)/np.median(a)-1)*100:.1f}%)',fontsize=11,pad=12)
 ax.set_ylim(0,max(a)*1.2)
fig.suptitle('Canoli Studio: unchanged native matting pixels, less solver time',fontsize=15)
fig.supxlabel('Sequential Node measurements on this container; dots are every eligible repeat. Same iterations and byte-identical neutral/default output.\nNot browser p95, input-to-photon, hardware GPU or whole-process peak-memory evidence. GT04 warmup pair 1 excluded; all raw runs retained.',fontsize=9)
fig.savefig('docs/benchmarks/matting-wasm-performance-2026-10-16.png',dpi=180,bbox_inches='tight',pad_inches=.2)
